root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 introduced two transformations to pdf_to_markdown_docling that are the ONLY code changes between Run 12 and Run 13 affecting markdown content: (1) _repair_docling_tables wrapping every export_to_markdown() call (converters.py:2388-2458, applied at lines 2627,2697,2991), and (2) NFKC normalization of Arabic Presentation Forms in _pre_inference_normalize (converters.py:2197-2200). Both SLA and marsoom-13 are Arabic PDFs flat-routed (tree <3 nodes). In Run 12, route_and_extract_flat produced 264 and 6 blocks respectively. In Run 13, 0 blocks. The markdown is non-empty (doc_description populates from metadata), but route_and_extract_flat produces zero parseable blocks from it — all content ends up skipped (likely via fence-toggle, HR-separator, or empty-line paths). The exact interaction causing total block loss needs per-document markdown comparison. qerar-106 shows a different pattern (truncation at Article 4, 179->11 nodes) but shares the Arabic extraction context.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:_repair_docling_tables (2388-2458) + converters.py:_pre_inference_normalize NFKC (2197-2200) -> pdf_to_markdown_docling (2627,2697) -> client.py:md_content -> flat routing -> route_and_extract_flat
root_causes.suggested_fix: Compare the markdown output of pdf_to_markdown_docling for the SLA doc with and without _repair_docling_tables and NFKC normalization (toggle via env vars RFC029_TABLE_DEDUP_ENABLED=0 and conditionalizing the NFKC block). Identify which transformation produces markdown that route_and_extract_flat cannot parse into blocks. Then fix the specific interaction — likely a table-row formatting change that causes the flat parser to misclassify content lines.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 added 4 new validate_tree failure reasons (suspect_density, low_content_density, empty_node_contamination, arabic_low_content_ratio) in helpers.py but NONE are handled in client.py's recovery/routing paths. OCR escalation only handles garbling/node_garbling/visual_order_garble. Flat routing only handles node_count<3/depth<2. These new reasons fall through to raise LowQualityTreeError (ERROR) with NO recovery opportunity. For docs in THIS cluster the tree has <3 nodes so node_count<3 fires first (before suspect_density), but the gap is systemic and explains the 3 ERROR docs in the audit (Penal Code, federal_decree_law_no_33, marsoom_33). For the SLA doc (20 pages, ~27k chars = ~1394 chars/page < 1500 threshold), suspect_density WOULD fire if the tree had >=3 nodes.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:validate_tree (1330-1375 new gates) -> client.py:index (1381-1639 — none of the 4 new reasons match flat routing or OCR escalation conditions)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add the new validate_tree failure reasons to either the OCR escalation condition or the flat routing condition in client.py. suspect_density and low_content_density should route to flat (reason='node_count<3') since the tree has content but is structurally rejected. empty_node_contamination should attempt OCR escalation. arabic_low_content_ratio should attempt OCR escalation.

root_causes.root_cause: Docling TableFormer cannot extract vector-icon table cells (checkmarks/symbols rendered as PDF path operators, not Unicode text glyphs). The Unfallversicherung benefit-comparison tables have empty_cell_ratio 0.44-0.75 because cell content is rasterized vector icons invisible to text-layer extraction. This predates RFC-029 and has persisted across all runs (Run 11, 12, 13). No RFC-029 change addresses this; _repair_docling_tables processes table FORMAT (dedup, whitespace) but cannot recover content Docling never extracted.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:pdf_to_markdown_docling -> Docling TableFormer ACCURATE mode -> export_to_markdown() (checkmark glyphs lost at extraction) -> helpers.py:_flat_parse_table -> helpers.py:flag_empty_cells
root_causes.suggested_fix: Cell-level rasterization+OCR for table cells with zero text content but non-zero visual content (vector-icon path operators). Alternative: Docling upstream enhancement for path-operator glyph recognition. RFC-010 originally scoped this; RFC-027 deferred it.
